# Build-only adapter patches

`upstream.js`, `upstream.css`, `upstream-host.css`, and LICENSE are immutable observed bytes. Pins are checked before parsing/transformation. Refresh requires recapture, contract review and explicit pin updates, never editing upstream to satisfy a test.

1. **factory-injection:** replace exactly one IIFE opener and SDK global lookup with `export function createNativeKanban(SDK, host)`. Check every required primitive/hook/service by name before creating the page. The original rendering and state functions remain in their closure.
2. **local-registration:** replace exactly one registry tail with `return KanbanPage`. Importing the module is inert. Invocation defines a component; it does not mount it or start requests. No SDK or registry is placed on any global.
3. **host-globals:** destructure window, document, navigator, WebSocket, URL, timers, animation-frame scheduler and console from the explicit host. Task 13 supplies leaf-scoped event/DOM/storage/download implementations with teardown. Task 16 composes state and drafts. The host translator and accepted DashboardClient jointly enforce the closed route inventory.
4. **scoped-styles:** compile native utilities from both immutable Kanban JS and the exact Nous component dependency graph. Preserve native host compatibility tokens. Prefix all outer selectors with `.hcv-kanban-root.hcv-kanban-root`; map html/body/:root/:host/#root to that container. The repeated class outranks stock Obsidian control-state selectors while preserving relative native recipe specificity. Nested rules remain nested within their scoped ancestor. Promote native named layers into unlayered output in first-declared layer order, before native unlayered overrides, so Obsidian's unlayered rules cannot dominate them solely through layer precedence. Unknown, nested and conditional layer structures fail the build. A base-layer shadow reset on buttons, inputs, selects and textareas prevents inherited host chrome; native utility shadows retain precedence. Native checkbox inputs restore browser appearance, transparent background, borderless chrome and the browser focus outline; their host-only checkmark pseudo-element is suppressed. The checkbox color scheme is explicitly `normal`, matching the reference document in both themes instead of inheriting Obsidian’s light/dark native-control palette. Native checked state and accent utilities remain authoritative. No new `!important` is added. Namespace CSS custom properties, @property registrations and keyframe names; rewrite primitive inline var references with the same mapping. No document reset escapes the leaf.
5. **host-fonts:** omit fonts.css and all native @font-face blocks. Map brand families to Obsidian interface/monospace fonts, with system fallbacks. Explicitly approved task-4 adaptation: glyphs and metrics differ; spacing/hierarchy/native controls remain. No font binaries are copied to output and no remote assets are loaded. Nous package MIT declaration establishes code licensing only; font rights remain unverified.
6. **no-view-transitions:** remove document navigation view transitions and their document pseudo-element rules. These are host-site navigation effects, not Kanban interactions.
7. **unused-optional-peers:** Nous utility/barrel modules reference Three, GSAP and Leva for unrelated 3D/control-panel functions. Mark these optional imports as side-effect-free externals so esbuild can eliminate their unused functions. Fail the standalone build if any external import survives. No replacement implementation is supplied, and any future control requiring one of these peers must fail until its dependency/license is reviewed.

Generated files are ignored, rebuilt before the plugin bundle, and include SHA receipts plus CSS utility coverage. The main plugin is unchanged; later composition imports factory.js and primitives.ts. The standalone `generated/primitives.mjs` is the build-proof package, and `generated/kanban.css` is the complete scoped sheet for later style composition. Package licenses and exact locked versions are emitted as `generated/license-inventory.json` and `generated/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt`.

Task 13 must import React, hooks, primitives and createRoot through `primitives.ts` in the same esbuild graph. Never combine the standalone proof bundle with another React instance. Use `React.createElement` in host TypeScript. Radix portals must receive a container inside the leaf root, and modal scroll locking/document style effects require scoped host integration before mounting. This task proves inert factory creation, not rendered portal containment.

Verification: run `bun run build && bun test tests/kanban-vendor.test.ts` only on the verified M1 isolated checkout. The tests corrupt temporary source/manifest/style/primitive inputs and reject them by name; they never alter immutable production copies. Full screen fidelity and host lifecycle are later tasks, not claims of this library build.

## Task 13 leaf adaptations

`build-host-patches.mjs` applies fail-closed exact replacements and a TypeScript AST control-removal pass to the verified source. Original files remain byte-identical. The native WS/backoff effect delegates to the injected sole `watch` owner; onEvents advances the native cursor only. The owner coalesces one onRefresh that directly reloads the board and invalidates the currently open detail through its native tick, including poll/reconnect/overflow. No extra host250ms delay is added. Completion prompts become awaited leaf dialogs, preserving cancellation and required summaries. Confirmation resolvers cancel on replacement/unmount. Touch hit-testing is leaf scoped, pointer ids are matched, cancel never drops, and ghost coordinates are relative to the leaf.

The removal pass excludes board administration, orchestration administration, trash/archive/delete, upload/remove-attachment, dispatch, specify/decompose, home-channel toggles, reclaim/reassign diagnostics and subscriptions. Read-only CLI hints copy text only; documentation actions are constrained to the Hermes HTTPS documentation origin. Unsupported transport routes remain denied even if invoked directly.

`build-orchestration-patches.mjs` retains the native orchestration panel for the approved `GET /orchestration` and `GET /profiles` reads. Configured and resolved roles, mode, profile descriptions and default/auto-review metadata remain visible in the native layout with a read-only label. Selectors, mode toggles, description editors and all PUT/PATCH/describe-auto handlers are removed; only expand/collapse and Reload remain actionable. Consumed response fields are checked against the pinned native API's string/boolean shapes before display. Loading or failed reads cannot be displayed as Manual or an empty profile list. Reload invalidates older request generations, and unmount invalidates pending callbacks. Descriptions render as escaped text, including multiline content. The closed SDK/client route policy remains unchanged.

`kanban-sdk-host.ts` uses the single primitives React export, a contained fixed-position root, and a signature-compatible local ConfirmDialog adapter without document portals or global scroll locking. Drawer dimensions use leaf percentages. The host owns lifetime cancellation, event/timer/animation-frame/object-URL cleanup and local board storage; the caller owns reconnect/poll and shared connection services. Native editors do not yet preserve task12 drafts; task16 binds those semantics. The fixture RPC is synthetic browser QA only, not installed Obsidian transport.

## Task 16 mounted view adaptations

`build-view-patches.mjs` runs after the host pass, using exact replacement counts and AST boundaries against the same pinned source. It injects a leaf-local draft context supplied through optional `SDK.view`; it adds no global SDK or storage. Task drawers are keyed by board/task, while refreshes retain their editor DOM. Board and detail request generations reject obsolete results. Explicit navigation and one direct refresh callback are connected to the mounted native page; onEvents remains cursor-only.

Title, body, assignee, priority, model free-text, comment, dependency selections and each column's create fields use memory-only task12 draft records. Incoming detail reads update the remote revision without replacing local input. Cancel clears the relevant explicit editor draft where the native action discards it; closing a drawer retains drafts for reopening. Failed/uncertain edits keep the editor open, comments and dependencies retain their input, and create failure retains its fields with a review warning. Successful field readback clears only matching submitted drafts. Comment/create completions cannot erase text edited while their request was pending. Native mutation request shapes, workflow, controls, lanes and transport denials are inherited unchanged.

Repair attempt2 routes external navigation through the native `switchBoard`, so cross-board selection, last-selection anchor, failed selections and filters reset before setting the requested drawer target. Same-board navigation/refresh does not reset them. Each mutation captures its submitted draft values before awaiting transport; readback may clear a field only while that exact value is still current and the actual persisted field matches the request. Native title/assignee/model trimming and priority number conversion are explicitly field-specific; body text is never trimmed. Editor success callbacks retain an editor when its input changed during the pending save.

`HermesKanbanView` mounts this factory once through the task13 host and adds quiet connection/board/freshness chrome. Composition owns styles, shared state/client/tunnel, visibility and guarded leaf close. `requestClose` is an asynchronous permission seam; `onClose` is forced teardown, not a public Obsidian veto hook. See the task16 interface evidence for the precise lifetime contract and remaining installed UI acceptance.

The existing leaf-host drawer/dialog containment stylesheet uses three root classes to outrank compiled two-root native recipes independently of style load order. The drawer height and maximum height resolve against the leaf-bound shade; its width keeps the namespaced native drawer-width variable and caps at 92% of the leaf. The dialog maximum height remains the existing leaf-relative calculation. The drawer close button alone restores its native automatic height instead of the host’s fixed input height; native line height, padding and states remain unchanged. Native drawer header, body scrolling and footer rules are unchanged.

The existing React target is the board scroll host. Its height is bounded by the leaf while the outer root remains the fixed-overlay containing block. When a native drawer or dialog is present, only the inner scroll host switches to overflow hidden; its scroll offsets are retained and normal board scrolling resumes on close. The inner host has no transform or containment, so opening an overlay after board scrolling still anchors it to the outer leaf.

Leaf-owned confirmation and prompt backdrops use scoped z-index 61 above the pinned native drawer shade at 60. Native reference Radix dialogs can appear behind that drawer while their inert background still permits modal input. The leaf adaptation deliberately keeps confirmation controls both visible and hittable, independent of sibling order; it does not reproduce that native visual stacking defect.

The leaf focus hook owns initial prompt focus after recording the opener; the prompt input does not preempt that capture with a second autofocus. A mousedown directly on either leaf backdrop prevents only the browser focus blur, keeping outside-click then Tab inside the existing local trap. Input/button events and dialog settlement remain unchanged.
Handled Escape in a leaf confirmation or prompt stops propagation before the native drawer window listener, so canceling the modal preserves its opener drawer. Escape with no leaf modal still reaches the native drawer.

The local Tab boundary also handles a focused dialog container (for example after clicking its title or padding). It wraps to the first or last enabled control, and retains container focus when loading disables every control. Initial focus chooses an enabled control or the dialog itself; the prompt form has a programmatic focus target so padding clicks stay inside this same boundary. No document-level focus listener is introduced.

Obsidian 1.12.7 dispatches its application Escape shortcut during window capture, before React receives the key. The view injects a supported Obsidian key scope while a leaf confirmation or prompt is open. It cancels only Escape originating inside that dialog, and falls through to the parent scope for other targets and keys. The focus effect releases the exact scope before restoring its opener; unmount/disposal also releases it, with an idempotent pop. No global DOM listener is added.

## Bulk completion summary contract (Task 22)

The pinned bulk Complete button promises a summary but emits only `status: done`; unlike the single-task path it never collects the required completion text. The existing host transformation now reuses `requestCompletionSummary` after native Apply confirmation, before optimistic movement or SDK dispatch, and forwards the trimmed text in both native `result` and `summary` fields. Cancelled or blank completion leaves tasks and selection unchanged. The native bulk endpoint, completion policy, per-ID result handling and authoritative board readback stay in their existing owners. This fulfills the approved adapted completion contract; the pinned reference's missing-prompt refusal is retained as a native defect characterization.

Each bulk invocation snapshots its selected IDs and board. A page-local generation invalidates pending confirmation, summary and response work when selection or board changes, another bulk operation starts, or the page unmounts. The successful current response retains native selection clearing and immediate readback; its own later render does not cancel that readback. No route, payload type, transport guard or immutable upstream source is changed.

## Card touch gesture ownership (Task 22)

The native card pointer handler starts a proxy after movement but has no pre-gesture touch-action policy. The actual small-step trace still cancels at 16px while the columns begin horizontal scrolling. The build CSS now declares `touch-action: pan-y pinch-zoom` on `.hermes-kanban-card[draggable="true"]`, which the existing stylesheet transformation confines to the Kanban leaf. This reserves horizontal card-origin gestures for the existing drag handler while permitting vertical pan and pinch. It does not constrain column backgrounds, the scroll host, drawer/editor controls or sibling leaves.

The policy applies to the whole native draggable card, including its bulk checkbox descendant; adding descendant `auto` would not undo the ancestor restriction. The existing native card contains title/id/meta content and that checkbox, with editors outside it. Keep the current movement threshold, checkbox click propagation, pointer-id checks, cancel-never-drop cleanup and native workflow/confirmation path. Actual sustained touch drop, checkbox/tap behavior, vertical card scrolling, background horizontal pan and desktop mouse drag require the separate QA acceptance run. This local preparation does not claim that run has passed.
